meta.filingRule: Save finished .csv and .json files in '600 Maturity Submissions'. Never move or delete files in that folder.

voc.definition: Short interviews with site leaders to capture the top 3 operational headaches the Lean programme must solve.

gateway-question.definition: One of the 17 starred questions that must score at least 3 across 70% of the site before higher-level questions count.

seventy-percent-rule.definition: A Lean habit must work across roughly 70% of the site to score 3 or higher. One pilot team does not count.

okr.definition: 2–3 clear Objectives paired with Key Results following the pattern: [Measure] from [Start] to [Target] by [Date].

TOL-001.name: Maturity Assessment & Explainer
TOL-001.purpose: Score all 28 site Lean questions in pairs, view plain-English Level 1–5 flashcards, and export your .json and .csv files.
gettingStarted: Book a 90-minute scoring session with your Lean Core Team partner—never score alone.
Open the Maturity Explainer flashcards alongside the 28 questions to check what Level 3 proof looks like.

quickCommands.command: Score >= 3 with real workplace proof across ~70% of site teams
Save Data.json and Data.csv inside folder: 600 Maturity Submissions

troubleshooting.symptom: We had a score of 4 last year, but the habit stopped when a manager left.
troubleshooting.cause: Workplace habits regressed below the 70% site threshold.
troubleshooting.fix: Lower the score honestly to match today's real workplace proof so you can focus help where needed.

TOL-002.name: Score Explainer, Metro Journey & 4 Pillars
TOL-002.purpose: Show leaders visually which Gateways passed or failed, where the Metro train stops, and how the 1–4 level cap works.
gettingStarted: Have your saved Assessment .json file ready to upload.
If uploading an Excel .csv file fails, run it through the CSV to JSON Fixer utility first.

quickCommands.goal: Export subway-style visual map for leaders

troubleshooting.symptom: High scores on Level 2 and Level 3 questions did not raise our 1.6 total score.
troubleshooting.cause: A Level 1 Gateway question (such as Q10) scored below 3, pausing all higher-level questions.
troubleshooting.fix: Open Score Explainer to spot the red Level 1 Gateway and raise it to 3 across 70% of teams.

TOL-003.name: Strategy Builder, Simulator & CSV Fixer
TOL-003.purpose: Simulate how fixing red Gateways raises your score and export a local site improvement plan without needing a full workshop.
gettingStarted: Load your site's .json assessment file into Strategy Builder or Simulator.

quickCommands.goal: Fix broken Excel semicolon CSV exports
quickCommands.command: Open Utilities → CSV to JSON Fixer → Convert ';' to clean .json

quickCommands.goal: Build a standalone local action plan
quickCommands.command: Select Pilot, Standardization, or System Integration for each gap → Click 'Export Plan'

troubleshooting.symptom: CSV file fails to load into Score Explainer or Strategy Builder.
troubleshooting.cause: Regional Excel settings saved semicolons (;) instead of commas (,).
troubleshooting.fix: Open CSV to JSON Fixer in Utilities and convert the file into a clean .json file.

TOL-004.name: Analysis Report & VOC Input
TOL-004.purpose: Turn low Maturity scores into suggested Stage 0–9 actions and capture leader interview priorities before the workshop.
TOL-004.accessUrl: Navigator Toolkit → Analysis Report / VOC Input
gettingStarted: Complete your Site Maturity Assessment and save your Data.json file before opening Analysis Report.
Schedule 20-minute pre-workshop interviews with key site leaders to ask for their top 3 operational headaches.

quickCommands.goal: Generate draft gap slides from Maturity JSON
quickCommands.command: Analysis Report → Upload .json → Add notes → Click 'Export to PowerPoint'

quickCommands.goal: Export leadership Voice of the Customer pack
quickCommands.command: VOC Input → Enter leader pain points → Download Briefing Pack.pptx & VOC Log.csv

troubleshooting.symptom: Leaders bring up 15 different priorities during interviews.
troubleshooting.cause: Unfiltered wish lists dilute the half-day workshop.
troubleshooting.fix: Group interview notes inside VOC Input into the Top 3 recurring operational problems.

TOL-005.name: Workshop Guide, Charter Input & Action Log
TOL-005.purpose: Facilitate the 3-part leadership workshop, lock 12-month OKRs into a 1-page Charter, and track monthly completion.
TOL-005.accessUrl: Navigator Toolkit → Workshop Guide / Charter & Action Log
gettingStarted: Have your Briefing Pack.pptx (Leader Needs) and Action Report.pptx (Maturity Gaps) ready on screen.

quickCommands.goal: Write a strong, measurable Key Result
quickCommands.command: Pattern: [Measure] from [Start] to [Target] by [Date] (e.g., 25% to 75% by Q3)
Open Action Log → Check off completed tasks and update owners with site leaders

troubleshooting.symptom: Team writes weak task goals like 'Train 30 people in problem solving'.
troubleshooting.cause: Measures attendance in a room instead of real shop-floor habit change.
troubleshooting.fix: Rewrite as a habit metric: 'Increase shift huddles solving issues within 48h from 25% to 75% by Q3'.

TOL-006.name: Visual Stand-Up Board (Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost)
TOL-006.purpose: Display shift targets vs. actuals in red and green, log frontline containment actions, and flag cross-team blockers.
TOL-006.accessUrl: Work Area Stand-Up Board / Digital Tier 1 Hub
gettingStarted: Update yesterday's safety, quality, delivery, and cost numbers 5 minutes before the shift horn.
Have red and green dry-erase markers or the digital Tier 1 touch screen unlocked.

quickCommands.command: Colour the cell Red + Write a 1-line root cause + Assign a 24h owner

quickCommands.goal: Flag a blocker for Tier 2 escalation
quickCommands.command: Attach a Red Escalation Tag when an issue breaches the 2-hour cell limit

troubleshooting.symptom: Tier 1 stand-up drags past 15 minutes into a 40-minute technical debate.
troubleshooting.cause: Engineers trying to solve complex root causes at the stand-up board.
troubleshooting.fix: Use the 60-Second Rule: log immediate containment on the board and book a separate 3-person problem-solving huddle right after.

TOL-007.name: Escalation Triage Filter & 24-Hour Countermeasure Log
TOL-007.purpose: Filter shift blockers down to a maximum of 3 critical escalations for Tier 2 and assign 24-hour leadership countermeasures.
TOL-007.accessUrl: Tier 2 Operations Board → Escalation & Countermeasure Log
gettingStarted: Collect red escalation cards from all Tier 1 boards at least 15 minutes before the 09:00 Tier 2 huddle.
Ensure engineering, quality, and warehouse leads are present at the Tier 2 board.

quickCommands.goal: Filter Tier 1 red tags before Tier 2
quickCommands.command: Keep only cross-department blockers -> Cap at Max 3 Escalations per shift

quickCommands.goal: Close the loop back to the shop floor
quickCommands.command: Write the agreed 24-hour countermeasure and owner directly on the Tier 1 board before 10:00

troubleshooting.symptom: Team leaders stop raising red blockers because nothing changes after Tier 2.
troubleshooting.cause: Escalated items disappear into management emails without feedback to the cell.
troubleshooting.fix: Enforce the 10:00 AM Feedback Rule: the Local Programme Manager walks back to the cell board to confirm the assigned owner and fix time.

PRC-001.title: Check Your Site's Current Score
PRC-001.whenToUse: Every quarter with a Lean Core Team partner.
PRC-001.cardOutput: Completed 28-question health check & local action plan.
PRC-001.userGoal: Score your site's 28 Lean questions fairly in pairs, verify real workplace proof across 70% of teams, and build a local improvement plan.
PRC-001.trigger: Quarterly site Lean health check or preparation before a leadership Navigator Workshop.
PRC-001.finalOutcome: Calibrated Data.json and Data.csv saved in '600 Maturity Submissions' plus a visual Metro Journey and local Strategy Builder plan.
PRC-001.valueAddCoaching: Treat the assessment as a helpful coaching conversation, never an audit. Lowering an old score when a habit stops is a win because it directs help to the real bottleneck.

stages.name: Score All 28 Questions Together in a Pair
stages.summary: Score together with a Core Team partner using the 70% site rule and real workplace proof.

stages.name: Check Starred Gateways & Build a Local Action Plan
stages.summary: See which starred Gateways cap your level, export the Metro Journey PDF, and build a local plan in Strategy Builder.

PRC-002.title: Run a Leadership Action Workshop
PRC-002.userGoal: Combine your site's Maturity gap scores with leadership business priorities to agree on a 1-page Charter, measurable goals, and a 12-month roadmap.
PRC-002.trigger: Site is ready to align leadership priorities and Lean resources for the next 6 to 12 months.
PRC-002.finalOutcome: Signed 1-Page Navigator Charter with 2–3 measurable Key Results, a Q1–Q4 Interactive Roadmap, and monthly tracking in the Action Log.
PRC-002.valueAddCoaching: Never walk into a Navigator Workshop with only Maturity scores. Pairing red Gateway gaps with the Site Leader's top 3 business headaches turns 'Lean tasks' into urgent business solutions.

stages.name: Prepare Gap Slides & Interview Site Leaders
stages.summary: Upload your site score .json into Analysis Report and interview site leaders to build the pre-workshop Briefing Pack.

stages.name: Facilitate the Workshop, Lock Goals & Track Monthly
stages.summary: Run the 3-part agenda, write measurable goals in Charter Input, and review monthly in Action Log.

PRC-003.title: Run Tier 1 Cell Stand-Up & Escalate to Tier 2
PRC-003.whenToUse: At the start of every shift across all operational cells.
PRC-003.cardOutput: Updated SQDC board, 24-hour containment owners & max 3 Tier 2 escalations.
PRC-003.userGoal: Run a crisp 15-minute shift stand-up that spots safety, quality, delivery, and cost misses immediately and escalates cross-team blockers within 2 hours.
PRC-003.trigger: Start of shift (5 minutes before shift handover horn) and 09:00 AM Tier 2 escalation review.
PRC-003.finalOutcome: Every red metric has a named 24-hour containment owner and cross-department blockers are resolved at Tier 2 with feedback to the cell by 10:00 AM.
PRC-003.valueAddCoaching: A stand-up board is an action trigger, not a wallpaper report. Keep discussion strictly on red misses—green metrics take five seconds.

stages.name: Prep Visual Board & Run 15-Minute Tier 1 Stand-Up
stages.summary: Update shift actuals 5 minutes before shift start and run the 15-minute cell stand-up focused on red misses.

stages.name: Triage Blockers to Tier 2 & Assign 24-Hour Countermeasures
stages.summary: Filter cross-department blockers down to at most 3 red tags for Tier 2 and close the loop back to the shop floor.

SOP-001.title: Calibrate and Score All 28 Site Questions in Pairs

kitBag.outputProduced: Raw scores.csv & Data.json in 600 Maturity Submissions

SOP-001.userGoal: Complete a fair, evidence-based 1–5 rating for all 28 Lean@GS questions and save the official submission files.
gettingStarted: Pair the Local Programme Manager with a Lean Core Team member—new or uncertified managers must never score alone.
Open the Maturity Assessment and Maturity Explainer side-by-side inside the PM Maturity Hub.
Gather physical evidence: team huddle boards, meeting logs, and 3–6 months of trend charts.

steps.action: Review each question in a pair and check the Maturity Explainer flashcards.
steps.detail: The Local Programme Manager and Lean Core Team partner review all 28 questions together before showing leaders.
steps.coachingTip: Treat scoring as a helpful coaching conversation to find where teams need support—never push just to chase a higher number.

visual.caption: 5-Step Calibration Flow — Step 1: Score in a Pair

elements.label: STEP 1: Score in a Pair (Programme Mgr + Core Team)
Rule: Never score alone • Certified Core Team partner required

annotation.label: 1. Always Score Together in a Pair

steps.action: Apply the 70% site rule before awarding any score of 3, 4, or 5.
steps.detail: A habit must be working across roughly 70% of the site with real boards and logs to score 3 or higher.
steps.coachingTip: One enthusiastic pilot area or a written slide deck that nobody uses scores a 2 (Just Starting), never a 3.

elements.label: Score 4: Daily Habit (3–6m trends) | Score 5: Self-Running

steps.action: Review draft scores with site leaders and update only when shown real proof.
steps.detail: Walk leaders through the draft ratings and adjust a score only if physical workplace evidence proves it.
steps.coachingTip: If a habit scored 4 last year but stopped working, lower the score openly so the site gets support to rebuild it.

elements.label: Required Proof: Working boards, meeting logs, 3-6 month action history

steps.action: Download the finished .json and .csv files into the 600 Maturity Submissions folder.
steps.detail: Never move, rename, or delete historical files inside the 600 Maturity Submissions folder.
steps.coachingTip: Always export both .json and .csv—the .json file loads cleanly into Score Explainer and Navigator Toolkit without Excel formatting bugs.

elements.label: ARCHIVE RULE: Never move or delete files in 600 Maturity Submissions

troubleshooting.symptom: A manager insists a single high-performing cell justifies a score of 3 for the whole site.
troubleshooting.cause: Confusing a local pilot (Score 2) with a site-wide standard (Score 3).
troubleshooting.fix: Point to the 70% Site Rule: score it 2 today and use Strategy Builder to scale that cell's standard to 70% of teams.

SOP-002.title: Diagnose Gateway Score Caps and Build a Local Action Plan

kitBag.outputProduced: Capped Maturity Score, Red Starred Gateways (★) & Metro PDF

SOP-002.userGoal: Identify which starred Gateway questions cap your site's level and export a targeted local action plan.
gettingStarted: Locate your saved Data.json file from your site assessment.
Open Score Explainer, Metro Journey, and Strategy Builder inside the PM Maturity Hub.

steps.action: Upload your .json file into Score Explainer to see which Gateways cap your level.
steps.detail: All 17 starred Gateway questions (★) in your level must score at least 3 before higher-level questions count.
steps.coachingTip: If Gateway #10 (Pilot Experiments) scores 2/5, your site is capped at Level 1 (e.g., 1.6/4.0) even if Level 2 questions score 4.

visual.caption: Gateway Score Cap — Why Q10 = 2/5 Caps Total Score at 1.6

elements.label: Score Explainer • Level Cap Formula: Level + [(Avg - 1) / 4]
Levels 2–4 Paused Until Q10 >= 3  •  Final Score: 1.6 / 4.0

steps.action: Open Metro Journey and click 'Save PDF' to show leaders where the train stops.
steps.detail: Pair the Metro Journey map with 'The 4 Pillars (Live)' view to highlight green PASS and red GAP badges.
steps.coachingTip: Leaders grasp the subway map in ten seconds—point directly to the red station blocking the train from advancing.

visual.caption: Phase 2: Visualize — Metro Journey & 4 Pillars Live

elements.label: Metro Line: L0 PASS ──● Q10 STOP
4 Pillars Live: Shows Green [PASS] and Red [GAP] Badges by Pillar

steps.action: Select actions for each red Gateway inside Strategy Builder and click 'Export Plan'.
steps.detail: Choose Pilot, Standardization, or System Integration for each gap and test the impact in Simulator.
steps.coachingTip: Fix current-level red Gateways first—raising Q10 from 2 to 3 immediately unlocks all 12 Level-2 questions.

visual.caption: Phase 3: Plan — Strategy Builder & Score Simulator

elements.label: Strategy Builder • Local Action Plan Generator
Simulator Preview: Fixing Q10 Unlocks Level 2 (1.6 → 2.6)

troubleshooting.symptom: Uploading the Excel .csv file into Score Explainer gives a format error.
troubleshooting.cause: Excel saved semicolons (;) instead of commas (,).
troubleshooting.fix: Click 'CSV to JSON Fixer' under Utilities in the PM Maturity Hub to convert the file to a clean .json.

SOP-003.title: Prepare the Navigator Workshop Inputs

kitBag.mandatoryStatus: MANDATORY FOR WORKSHOP • OPTIONAL FOR STANDALONE CHECK
kitBag.inputNeeded: Site Maturity Data.json + Short Leader Interviews
kitBag.outputProduced: Action Report.pptx + VOC Briefing Pack (Safety, Delivery, Quality, Cost)

SOP-003.userGoal: Prepare the two mandatory workshop inputs: the Maturity Gap Action Report and the Leader Priorities Briefing Pack.
gettingStarted: Have your completed Site Maturity Data.json file ready.
Complete short 1-on-1 interviews with site leaders to ask for their top 3 business headaches.

steps.action: Upload your site score .json file into Analysis Report and click 'Export to PowerPoint'.
steps.detail: Review the suggested actions across Stages 0–9 and add local Lean Core Team notes before exporting.
steps.coachingTip: Highlight the exact 2 or 3 red Gateway questions that block the next maturity level so leaders don't drown in all 28 questions.

steps.action: Type leader interview pain points into VOC Input and download the Briefing Pack.
steps.detail: Downloads both the VOC Log.csv and the pre-workshop Briefing Pack.pptx showing leadership's top priorities.
steps.coachingTip: Use the leaders' own words for lead-time delays, repeat quality defects, or handoff friction so they immediately recognize their priorities in the room.

troubleshooting.symptom: Site leaders want to skip pre-workshop interviews to save time.
troubleshooting.fix: Do a 10-minute hallway or phone check for just their top 3 headaches—entering the workshop without leader priorities turns the meeting into a debate.

SOP-004.title: Facilitate the Half-Day Workshop, Write Goals, and Track Monthly

kitBag.inputNeeded: Top 5 Prioritised Actions + VOC Briefing Pack
kitBag.outputProduced: Signed 1-Page Charter, Measurable OKRs & Active 90-Day Coaching Plan

SOP-004.userGoal: Guide leaders through the 3-part agenda, lock 2–3 measurable goals into the 1-Page Charter, and track monthly in Action Log.
gettingStarted: Open Workshop Guide on the main projector screen with the Site Leader Sponsor and Lean Core Team.
Have Charter Input and Interactive Roadmap open in adjacent tabs to capture decisions live.

steps.action: Run Part 1 (45m) and Part 2 (60m) to connect leader problems to failed Gateways.
steps.detail: Part 1 locks the Top 3 business problems; Part 2 connects those problems to red Gateway gaps.
steps.coachingTip: Show how fixing Gateway #10 (Pilot Experiments) or #14 (Daily Huddles) directly solves the leader's lead-time or defect headache.

elements.label: Workshop Guide • Live Half-Day Session Agenda
Next: Part 3 (75m) Agree on 2–3 Programme Objectives & Key Results

steps.action: Write 2–3 Objectives and measurable Key Results inside Charter Input during Part 3 (75m).
steps.detail: Follow the strict goal pattern: [Measure] from [Start] to [Target] by [Date], then place tasks into Q1–Q4.
steps.coachingTip: Never write 'Train 30 people'. Write: 'Increase daily shift huddles solving issues within 48h from 25% to 75% by Q3'.

visual.caption: Navigator Step 5 (CREATE) — Charter Input & Strong Goal Pattern

elements.label: Also Lock KR 1.1: Raise Gateway #10 from 2/5 to 3/5 across 70% by Q2

steps.action: Download the 1-Page Charter poster and review progress monthly inside Action Log.
steps.detail: Open Charter & Roadmaps to export the Final Deck.pptx, then track task completion monthly in Action Log.
steps.coachingTip: Book the first three monthly 30-minute Action Log check-ins before leaders leave the workshop room.

visual.caption: Navigator Step 6 (COMMUNICATE) — 1-Page Charter & Monthly Action Log

elements.label: Step 6 • Charter & Roadmaps + Monthly Action Log
Sustains Momentum for 6–12 Months Until Next Site Re-Assessment

troubleshooting.symptom: Workshop discussion gets stuck debating a single question score from the site check.
troubleshooting.cause: Re-litigating individual scores instead of focusing on strategic bottlenecks.
troubleshooting.fix: Remind the room that scores were calibrated in pairs; pivot immediately to which red Gateway blocks the leader's top 3 priorities.

SOP-005.title: Prep Visual Board Metrics and Run the 15-Minute Tier 1 Stand-Up
SOP-005.stationLocation: Cell SQDC Stand-Up Board (5 mins before shift)

kitBag.outputProduced: Updated SQDC Board & Immediate Containment Actions

SOP-005.userGoal: Update Safety, Quality, Delivery, and Cost metrics before shift start and run a sharp 15-minute stand-up that assigns containment actions to every red miss.
gettingStarted: Arrive at the cell board 5 minutes before the shift handover horn with the outgoing shift log.
Ensure green and red markers (or digital status tiles) are ready before calling the team together.

steps.action: Write yesterday's safety, quality, delivery, and cost numbers on the board before shift starts.
steps.detail: Mark each metric green when it meets target or red when it misses target.
steps.coachingTip: Never waste stand-up time writing numbers while the team watches—have every metric colored red or green 5 minutes early.

visual.caption: Stage 1 — Prep Visual SQDC Board 5 Minutes Before Shift

elements.label: Tier 1 Visual Stand-Up Board • Pre-Shift Check (-5 Mins)
Rule: All SQDC cells must be colored Red or Green before the horn sounds

annotation.label: 1. Mark Missed Targets in Red Early

steps.action: Walk through Safety, Quality, Delivery, and Cost in 15 minutes focusing on red misses.
steps.detail: Spend five seconds acknowledging green targets and focus discussion on red misses and today's risks.
steps.coachingTip: Stand physically in front of the board—when the leader touches the red number on the board, the whole team focuses on the gap.

elements.label: 15-Minute Tier 1 Huddle • Focus on Red Exceptions
Strict Timebox: 15 Minutes Max • Park deep root-cause debates for offline

steps.action: Write a named owner and 24-hour fix time next to every red item.
steps.detail: If the team cannot fix a blocker within 2 hours, attach a Red Escalation Tag for Tier 2.
steps.coachingTip: Never write 'Team' as the owner—write a single person's name and exact hour when the check will happen.

visual.caption: Stage 2 Output — Immediate Containment & Red Tag Trigger

elements.label: Tier 1 Action Strip • Single Owner & 24-Hour Due Time
Handoff: Red Escalation Tags move to Tier 2 Triage before 09:00 AM

troubleshooting.symptom: Team members stay silent when asked about obstacles on the shift.
troubleshooting.cause: Questions are too vague ('Any issues?') instead of pointing to a specific target condition.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask a direct target-condition question: 'We lost 40 minutes on station 3 yesterday—what blocked the handoff?'

SOP-006.title: Filter Blockers to Tier 2 and Close the 24-Hour Countermeasure Loop

kitBag.leadRole: Local Programme Manager (LPM) & Site Leadership Sponsor
kitBag.outputProduced: Max 3 Escalated Red Blockers & Signed Countermeasure Log

SOP-006.userGoal: Filter Tier 1 red tags down to a maximum of 3 critical cross-department escalations and lock 24-hour leadership countermeasures.
gettingStarted: Gather all Red Escalation Tags from the Tier 1 boards 15 minutes before the 09:00 AM Tier 2 meeting.
Open the Escalation Triage Filter to separate cell-level fixes from true cross-department blockers.

steps.action: Filter incoming Tier 1 red tags down to at most three cross-department blockers.
steps.detail: Return local single-team issues to the cell leader and keep only safety, quality, or delivery stops needing cross-team help.
steps.coachingTip: Escalating ten minor items paralyzes Tier 2—capping escalations at three forces leaders to solve the real bottleneck today.

visual.caption: Stage 3 — Escalation Triage Filter (Max 3 Red Blockers)

elements.label: Local Cell Issue → Return to Tier 1
Priority Order: 1. Safety Stop -> 2. Customer Line Stop -> 3. Quality Hold

steps.action: Assign a support department owner and 24-hour countermeasure for each escalated blocker.
steps.detail: The Site Leadership Sponsor assigns engineering, quality, or logistics leads to clear the obstacle within 24 hours.
steps.coachingTip: Confirm the support owner physically visits the shop-floor cell before noon rather than replying by email.

elements.label: Sponsor Sign-Off: Verifies resource commitment at the Tier 2 board

steps.action: Walk back to the cell board before 10:00 AM and write the agreed fix time.
steps.detail: Close the communication loop so frontline operators see their escalated blocker has an active owner.
steps.coachingTip: Nothing builds frontline trust faster than seeing a Tier 2 countermeasure written on their cell board within an hour.

elements.label: Close the Loop • Tier 2 Back to Tier 1 Cell Board
Output: Signed Countermeasure Log & Verified Cell Feedback

annotation.label: 3. Post Fix Time on Cell Board <10:00

troubleshooting.symptom: Tier 2 board is flooded with 12 red tags every morning.
troubleshooting.cause: Tier 1 leaders are escalating issues before attempting a 2-hour cell containment.
troubleshooting.fix: Use the Escalation Triage Filter before the meeting to return cell-fixable items and enforce the Max 3 Red Blockers cap.

questions28.text: Is there a clear business reason driving this Lean Programme?
Is leadership committed and actively invested in being involved?
Has the team or organisation started acquiring foundational Lean knowledge?
How clearly can your team describe what Lean means and how it supports your business goals?
How deeply do team members understand core Lean concepts?
Is there a consistent and active plan to close competency gaps?
Is there a clear Lean structure and defined role ownership within the team?
How effectively is strategy managed and reviewed at your level?
How well are strategic objectives cascaded to teams?
Does the team actively execute structured, pilot experiments?
Are Lean tools routinely applied and embedded in daily operations?
Are performance metrics and Lean-relevant KPIs displayed and actively discussed in the work area?
Is the review of KPIs driven by Lean principles to prevent local optimization?
Are daily huddles used consistently to raise and resolve issues?
How effectively are employee suggestions captured and implemented?
Does the team practice structured reflection?
How consistently are lessons learned documented and applied?
Does your Lean philosophy extend across your entire value chain?
Are internal departmental handoffs integrated to ensure seamless process flow?
Do leaders practice the 'Gemba Walk' habit consistently?
Do leaders use a consistent questioning cycle to identify target conditions and obstacles?
Is there a culture of psychological safety that encourages safe experimentation?
Are learnings from reflection used to update standard work?
Is physical verification used to validate pilot project outcomes?
Are successful standards systematically scaled across the site?
Do teams from different functions collaborate to improve shared processes?
Are joint improvement projects executed with external partners?
How consistently are success stories shared and replicated?

playbooks.title: The Lean@GS Navigator & Maturity Process
playbooks.subtitle: A practical journey from understanding your organisation's current Lean capability to agreeing what Lean should actually do for the business. Note: The maturity assessment is not the Navigator process—it is one of Navigator's two principal inputs.

goldenPrinciple.quote: The goal isn't to improve the maturity score. The goal is to improve the business.
goldenPrinciple.explanation: The Maturity Assessment tells you what capability you have and what may need developing. The Voice of the Customer tells you what the business needs. Navigator brings the two together so your organisation can decide where Lean should focus.

rulesKey.title: Before You Start: 3 Helpful Principles for Scoring & Prioritising
rulesKey.subtitle: How the Maturity Assessment & Navigator work together

items.desc: Complete the 28 questions openly with your leadership team and Lean Core Team partner to spot where support is needed—never chase a higher number for its own sake.
To score a 3 or higher, a working habit should be visible with real boards and routines across roughly 7 out of 10 teams—a single pilot area scores a 2.

items.term: 🎯 3. Focus on 2–3 Key Actions at a Time
items.desc: Avoid building a 28-item wishlist. Combine your capability gaps with business needs to focus on 2 or 3 high-impact actions at a time.

journeyMap.formulaBanner: Assess capability → Analyse gaps → Understand business priorities → Align the two with leadership → Agree objectives & initiatives → Build the action plan
journeyMap.briefingTitle: 60-Second Leadership Briefing: How Maturity & Navigator Fit Together
journeyMap.briefingEquation: Input 1: Lean Capability (Stages 1–2) + Input 2: Business Need (Stage 3) = Agreed 1-Page Charter & Action Plan (Stages 4–6)
briefingBullets: 1. The goal isn't to improve the maturity score—the goal is to improve the business.
2. Stages 1 & 2 show our current Lean capability and highlight 2–3 key gaps; Stage 3 captures the Voice of the Customer (the business problems leadership needs solved).
3. In Stages 4 to 6, we bring both inputs into the Navigator Workshop, agree a 1-Page Charter with clear objectives, and convert it into an owned action plan.

stages.title: Establish the Baseline (Assess)

stages.title: Understand the Gaps (Analyse)

stages.outputArtifact: Focused view of 2–3 priority capability gaps to develop

stages.title: Understand the Business Need (Voice of the Customer)
stages.summary: Engage leadership and stakeholders to understand their critical business challenges, pain points, measures of breakthrough success, and the problems they need Lean to help solve.
stages.whoIsInvolved: LPM + Site Leadership / Stakeholders (with Core Team support)
stages.toolLabel: Navigator Toolkit (Voice of the Customer Input)
stages.outputArtifact: Clear business priorities & leadership pain points

stages.title: Bring the Two Together (Navigator Workshop)
stages.summary: Bring your Lean capability insights (Stages 1–2) and business needs (Stage 3) into the leadership workshop to establish why we are using Lean, the current situation, and our strategic plan.
stages.whoIsInvolved: Site Leadership Team + LPM + Lean Core Team Facilitator
stages.outputArtifact: Aligned strategic direction connecting Lean to business problems

stages.title: Agree What to Focus On (Charter)
stages.summary: Translate workshop agreement into clear objectives, key results, and supporting initiatives—along with your local improvement team, sponsor, and coaching roles.
stages.whoIsInvolved: Site Sponsor + LPM + Lean Core Team

stages.title: Convert Into Action (Roadmap & Action Plan)
stages.summary: Assign clear owners and target dates to your agreed initiatives. Present and manage your roadmap in the visual format that works best for your local organisation.
stages.whoIsInvolved: Local Programme Manager + Action Owners + Core Team Coach
stages.toolLabel: Navigator Action Log & Local Visual Roadmap
stages.outputArtifact: Active improvement plan with owners, dates, and coaching cadence

decisionTools.title: How Gateway Score Caps Work
decisionTools.subtitle: Why high scores on Level 2–4 questions do not raise your total score if a Level 1 Starred Gateway (such as Q10: Pilot Experiments) scores below 3.
decisionTools.stepsTitle: How Your Site Score Is Worked Out
steps: 1. Check Starred Gateways: Find the highest level where every starred Gateway question scored at least 3.
2. Count Unlocked Questions: Only include questions up to your unlocked level (e.g., 10 of 28 questions at Level 1).
3. Find the Average: Divide total points by unlocked questions (34 ÷ 10 = 3.40).
4. Apply Level Cap: Level + [(Average - 1) / 4] keeps your final score inside your unlocked level (1.6).

playbooks.title: Tiered Daily Management & Escalation Meetings
playbooks.subtitle: Run crisp 15-minute shift stand-up meetings, filter cross-department blockers down to at most 3 red tags, and lock 24-hour countermeasures.

goldenPrinciple.quote: The goal of a daily stand-up isn't to report numbers. The goal is to unblock the shift.
goldenPrinciple.explanation: Green metrics take five seconds. Spend your 15 minutes assigning clear 24-hour owners to cell-level misses and escalating at most three cross-department blockers to Tier 2.

rulesKey.title: Before You Start: The 3 Rules of Tiered Daily Management
rulesKey.subtitle: How shift stand-ups and escalations work in plain English

items.desc: Update numbers 5 minutes before the horn. Spend 5 seconds on green metrics and focus the 15-minute stand-up strictly on red misses.
If a cell team cannot contain a safety, quality, or delivery obstacle within 2 hours, attach a Red Escalation Tag for Tier 2.
Filter Tier 2 escalations to at most 3 critical cross-team blockers per shift and write the agreed fix time back on the cell board by 10:00 AM.

journeyMap.formulaBanner: Spot Red Exceptions Early → Contain in Cell (<2h) → Triage Max 3 Blockers to Tier 2 → Close Loop by 10:00 AM
journeyMap.briefingTitle: 60-Second Floor Briefing: Why We Run Tier 1 & Tier 2 Stand-Ups
journeyMap.briefingEquation: 5-Min Board Prep + 15-Min Red-Miss Focus + Max 3 Tier 2 Red Tags = 24-Hour Countermeasure Loop
briefingBullets: 1. Where we are: Every shift starts with a 15-minute check at the visual SQDC board—numbers are colored Red or Green 5 minutes before the horn so we never waste meeting time writing.
2. What matters: We don't debate root causes at the stand-up board. Cell-fixable misses get a named 24-hour owner; cross-team blockers breaching 2 hours get a Red Escalation Tag.
3. Our next step: The Local Programme Manager filters red tags down to a maximum of 3 critical blockers for the 09:00 AM Tier 2 huddle and writes the agreed fix back on the cell board by 10:00 AM.
